critiques.title: Expose exact monthly values on the velocity trend
critiques.issue: The velocity chart shows two lines but provides no hover detail for exact completed and target values by month.
critiques.rationale: In an exploratory dashboard, users need exact values to verify whether a department is merely close to target or materially behind it.

critiques.suggestion: Add a tooltip with month, series, and summed value so users can inspect exact monthly performance.

critiques.title: Bring burndown into the department exploration flow
critiques.issue: The department filter and bar-chart cross-filter update three views, but the burndown chart stays outside that comparison workflow.
critiques.rationale: When users isolate a department, leaving burndown fixed at the all-departments level breaks the dashboard's cross-view comparison and makes it harder to judge whether a specific team's workload is also burning down poorly.
critiques.evidence: The department filter targets task-velocity, department-tasks, and project-status, but not sprint-burndown; sprint-burndown's data also has no department field to participate in the same interaction.
critiques.suggestion: Add department granularity to the burndown view so it can respond to the same department selection as the other charts.

critiques.title: Give the cross-department comparison view the primary position
critiques.issue: The upper-left slot is occupied by the monthly trend chart, while the clearest cross-department comparison view sits to its right.
critiques.rationale: If the goal is to identify which teams need intervention, the department comparison chart is the fastest entry point because it shows all departments side by side and already drives filtering for the other views.
critiques.evidence: The upper-left tile is task-velocity, while department-tasks is the only chart that directly compares departments and acts as the cross-filter source.
critiques.suggestion: Reflow the board so the department comparison chart owns the upper-left hero position and the supporting charts follow from it.

critiques.title: Reduce reliance on color-only status identification
critiques.issue: Project status is distinguished only by slice color and a separate legend, so users must map colors back and forth to identify categories.
critiques.rationale: Color-only category decoding increases lookup effort and weakens accessibility, especially in a compact radial chart where slice comparison is already harder than in linear views.
critiques.evidence: The donut encodes status by color, keeps the legend on the right, and shows no in-mark text labels.
critiques.suggestion: Keep the donut but add concise value labels on slices while preserving the existing legend and color mapping.

critiques.title: Use a bar chart for status comparison instead of a donut
critiques.issue: The project status view uses angle and area to compare four categories, which makes small differences between statuses harder to judge than they need to be.
critiques.rationale: Managers comparing risk states across departments need precise category comparison more than a part-to-whole motif, especially when the same view also responds to department filtering.
critiques.evidence: project-status is an arc chart with theta encoding for summed value across On Track, At Risk, Blocked, and Completed.
critiques.suggestion: Switch the status distribution to a sorted bar chart so the relative counts of risk states are easier to compare.

critiques.title: Show the chart subtitles that are already defined
critiques.issue: Each tile has an authored subtitle in the board metadata, but chart subtitles are globally hidden, so useful interaction and interpretation cues are not visible on the dashboard.
critiques.rationale: Because this is an exploratory dashboard, short per-chart guidance is valuable when it explains filter behavior or what the measure represents; hiding already-authored subtitles removes that help without reducing chart count or complexity elsewhere.
critiques.evidence: All four tiles include subtitle text in board metadata, yet board.showChartSubtitles is false and each tile reports hasSubtitle false.
critiques.suggestion: Turn on chart subtitles so the existing explanatory text appears with each view.

critiques.title: Document refresh cadence and metric ownership outside the canvas
critiques.issue: The dashboard presents operational health metrics but the review packet contains no visible source, freshness, or ownership information for maintaining them over time.
critiques.rationale: For monitoring dashboards, unclear stewardship can erode trust even when the current visuals render correctly.
critiques.evidence: No maintenance or metric-governance information is present in the supplied dashboard evidence.
critiques.suggestion: Establish and document who owns each metric, how often the dashboard refreshes, and how exceptions or stale data are handled.
